turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Thank you. Well, I guess what pushed me to make this appointment is that I'm having a lot of trouble following through on things at work. 

I keep starting follow-up items after my audits, or after mentorship events, with every intention of finishing them. I really mean to. But then I'll find out days later that the final email, or a review note, or a form just... never actually got done. It's happening a lot lately, and it's starting to affect my job, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient explicitly states having trouble following through on things at work and failing to finish tasks like emails, review notes, or forms.

turns.doctor_question: How much distress or anxiety do you feel about not being able to complete these tasks at work?
turns.patient_response:
I don't know if I'd call it anxiety, exactly. I mean, I'm not panicking or anything like that. It's more just... really frustrating. 

It's stressful because I know I'm capable of doing the work, and I just look careless to my team when a simple review note doesn't get cleared. So, it definitely bothers me, but I wouldn't say I have actual anxiety about it. Just enough frustration that I knew I needed to figure out what's going wrong.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient mentions looking 'careless' to their team because they fail to clear simple review notes, indicating careless mistakes or inattention to detail.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies experiencing actual anxiety or panic regarding their work difficulties.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself easily distracted while working on these tasks?
turns.patient_response: Yes, very easily. If I'm trying to review an audit file, almost anything can pull me completely off track. It could be a Slack ping, someone talking outside my office, or even just... a random thought about my marathon training. Once my attention shifts, it's really hard to get back to the file I was working on.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient notes that once their attention shifts, it is very difficult to return to the task, indicating trouble sustaining attention.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient confirms being easily pulled off track by external stimuli like Slack pings or conversations, as well as unrelated thoughts about marathon training.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find your mind wandering or having trouble staying focused in situations outside of work as well?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. But honestly, I notice it most whenever I have to sit through anything lengthy, even other things at work. 

Like, I can start a long client meeting or an AI-tool training and be fully engaged at first. But after a while... my mind just slips off. I'll suddenly realize I've missed the last few minutes of what was being said, even though I'm still sitting there looking right at the screen. It's like my brain just checks out without my permission.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly confirms having trouble staying focused and describes their mind slipping off during lengthy tasks like meetings or trainings.

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling when you're in situations where you feel frustrated about not completing tasks?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't get anything like that. Like I mentioned earlier, it's not really a panic feeling for me. My heart doesn't race, and I don't get sweaty or shaky or anything. It's just... more of a mental annoyance with myself, rather than any kind of physical reaction.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel guilty about things that happen in your daily life?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I don't walk around feeling guilty about things in my daily life. I mean, I get frustrated when I can't finish an audit on time or when I zone out during a meeting, but it's not a deep sense of guilt. It's just irritation that I can't seem to stay on track.

symptom_reasoning.S030: The patient explicitly denies feeling a deep sense of guilt about things in their daily life.

Like I said, I definitely get annoyed with myself when I make careless mistakes at work or can't seem to just sit down and finish a task, but I know I'm capable. It's just... a struggle to get my brain to cooperate sometimes, not a feeling that I'm worthless or anything like that.

turns.patient_response: Yes, it's actually been a lifelong thing. My mother still jokes about it—she says I could ace a test with no problem, but then I'd completely forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack.
